name: Southwestern black bean and quinoa salad
side: Warm corn tortillas on the side.
steps: Put the quinoa in a saucepan with 2 cups water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for 15 minutes, until the water is absorbed. Let it stand 5 minutes, fluff with a fork and spread it on a plate to cool.
Heat a dry skillet over medium-high heat and cook the corn for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until it browns in spots. Tip it into a large bowl.
Whisk the lime juice, olive oil, cumin and salt together in the bowl with the corn.
Add the quinoa, black beans, bell pepper, cherry tomatoes, red onion and cilantro and toss well.
Wipe the skillet and warm the tortillas in it for about 30 seconds a side; wrap them in a clean towel.
Gently fold in the avocado, scatter the feta over the top and serve with the warm tortillas. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

name: Roasted carrot and lentil bowls with tahini yogurt
side: Warm pita wedges for scooping.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Put the lentils in a saucepan with 4 cups water, bring to a boil and simmer 20 to 25 minutes, until tender but not falling apart; drain.

Meanwhile toss the carrots and cauliflower on a sheet pan with 2 tbsp of the olive oil, the cumin and ¾ tsp of the salt. Roast 25 to 30 minutes, stirring once, until browned at the edges and tender when pierced with a knife.
Stir the Greek yogurt, tahini, half the lemon juice, the garlic, ¼ tsp salt and 2 tbsp water together until smooth.
Toss the hot drained lentils with the spinach, the rest of the lemon juice, the last 1 tbsp olive oil and ¼ tsp salt so the spinach wilts.
Warm the pita in the oven for the last 3 minutes of roasting.
Divide the lentils among bowls, top with the roasted vegetables, a big spoonful of tahini yogurt and the parsley, and serve with the pita.

name: Asparagus, pea and goat cheese frittata
side: Crusty bread and a lemony arugula salad.

ingredients.note: woody ends snapped off, cut in 1-inch pieces

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Whisk the eggs, milk, lemon zest, ¾ tsp salt and the pepper in a bowl.

Heat 1 tbsp of the olive oil in a 10-inch oven-safe skillet over medium heat. Add the asparagus and cook 4 minutes, stirring, until bright green and just tender. Stir in the peas and scallions for 1 minute.
Pour in the eggs, stir once to spread the vegetables, and dot the goat cheese over the top. Cook without stirring for 3 to 4 minutes, until the edges begin to set.
Move the skillet to the oven and bake 12 to 15 minutes, until the center is set and no longer jiggles and a knife comes out clean.
While it bakes, toss the arugula with the lemon juice, the last 1 tbsp olive oil and ¼ tsp salt.
Let the frittata rest 5 minutes, then cut into wedges and serve with the salad and crusty bread. Use an oven mitt on the hot handle.

name: Sesame tofu chopped salad with edamame
side: Brown rice on the side for the hungriest eaters.

ingredients.note: pressed dry, cut in ¾-inch cubes

steps: Toss the tofu cubes with 1 tbsp of the soy sauce, then with the cornstarch until coated.
Heat the neutral oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the tofu 8 to 10 minutes, turning every couple of minutes, until golden and crisp on most sides. Drain on a paper towel.
Meanwhile bring a small pot of water to a boil, cook the edamame 4 minutes, then drain and rinse under cold water.
Whisk the remaining 2 tbsp soy sauce, the rice vinegar, sesame oil, honey and ginger in a large bowl.
Add the cabbage, carrots, cucumber, scallions and edamame to the bowl and toss well with the dressing.
Pile the salad onto plates, top with the crispy tofu and sprinkle with sesame seeds.

name: Lemony chickpea, carrot and kale soup
side: Toasted crusty bread rubbed with garlic.
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots, celery and salt and cook 8 minutes, stirring, until the onion is soft.
Stir in the garlic for 1 minute, then add the broth and chickpeas and bring to a boil.
Add the orzo and simmer 8 minutes, stirring now and then so it doesn't stick.
Stir in the kale and simmer 3 to 4 minutes more, until the kale is tender and the orzo is cooked.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the lemon zest and juice. Taste and add more salt if needed.
Ladle into bowls, top with parmesan and serve with the toasted bread. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours; the orzo will soak up broth, so add a splash of water when reheating.

name: Smoky lentil and sweet potato soup
side: A dollop of Greek yogurt and warm cornbread or tortillas.
mildNote: Use 1 tsp smoked paprika; it's smoky rather than hot, and the yogurt cools it further.
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and bell pepper with the salt for 6 to 7 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the garlic, smoked paprika and cumin and cook 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the lentils, sweet potato, diced tomatoes and broth. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat, partly cover and simmer 25 to 30 minutes, until the lentils and sweet potato are tender.
Mash some of the sweet potato against the side of the pot to thicken the soup, then stir in the spinach until it wilts, about 1 minute.
Serve in bowls topped with a spoonful of Greek yogurt. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

name: Poached eggs over garlic yogurt with spiced chickpeas
side: Warm pita and a cucumber-tomato salad.
mildNote: Leave out the chili flakes; the sweet paprika butter is still full of flavor.
steps: Stir the Greek yogurt, garlic and ½ tsp salt together and spread it over 4 shallow bowls. Toss the cucumber and tomatoes with a pinch of salt and half the dill.

Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat and fry the chickpeas 6 to 8 minutes, shaking the pan, until golden. Add the butter, and once it foams stir in the paprika and chili flakes and take it off the heat.
Bring a wide pan of water to a gentle simmer and add the vinegar. Crack each egg into a cup and slide 4 of them into the water.

Poach 3 to 4 minutes, until the whites are completely set and the yolks are thickened but soft (cook 1 to 2 minutes longer for firm yolks). Lift out with a slotted spoon onto a paper towel, then poach the other 4.
Set 2 eggs on each bowl of yogurt, spoon the chickpeas and spiced butter over the top and scatter with the rest of the dill.
Serve with the warm pita and the cucumber-tomato salad.

name: Tofu and black bean scramble tacos
side: Salsa, lime wedges and sliced avocado.
mildNote: Use mild salsa and halve the chili powder; most chili powder blends are gentle.
steps: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the bell peppers and onion 6 minutes, until soft and browned at the edges.
Crumble the tofu into the pan with your hands into small curds. Add the cumin, chili powder, turmeric and salt and cook 5 minutes, stirring, until the tofu is hot and lightly golden.
Stir in the black beans and spinach with 2 tbsp water and cook 2 minutes, until the beans are hot and the spinach wilts.
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet or directly over a low gas flame for about 30 seconds a side, then wrap in a towel.
Fill the tortillas with the scramble and top with salsa, avocado and a squeeze of lime.

name: Zucchini boats with lentils, tomato and mozzarella
side: A green salad and crusty bread.
steps: Simmer the lentils in 3 cups water for 20 to 25 minutes, until tender, then drain. Heat the oven to 400°F.

Scoop the centers out of the zucchini halves with a spoon, leaving a ¼-inch wall, and chop the scooped flesh. Lay the shells cut side up on a sheet pan, brush with 1 tbsp of the olive oil, sprinkle with ¼ tsp salt and bake 10 minutes.
Meanwhile heat ½ tbsp olive oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion and chopped zucchini 6 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic and Italian seasoning for 1 minute.
Stir in the lentils, marinara and ½ tsp salt and simmer 3 minutes, until thick.
Pile the filling into the zucchini shells, top with the mozzarella and parmesan and bake 15 minutes, until the cheese is melted and the zucchini is tender when pierced.
Toss the romaine with the vinegar and the last ½ tbsp olive oil. Scatter basil over the zucchini boats and serve with the salad.

name: Butternut squash and black bean chili
side: Greek yogurt, cilantro and tortilla chips on top.
mildNote: Use 2 tsp chili powder; the sweet squash keeps it gentle for kids.

ingredients.note: peeled, seeded, cut in ¾-inch cubes

steps: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and bell pepper with the salt for 7 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the garlic, chili powder and cumin and cook 1 minute, until fragrant.

Add the squash, black beans, crushed tomatoes and broth. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat, partly cover and simmer 25 to 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until the squash is tender when pierced with a fork.
Mash a few cubes of squash against the side of the pot to thicken the chili. Taste and add more salt if needed.
Serve in bowls topped with Greek yogurt, cilantro and a few crushed tortilla chips. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

name: Vegetarian Cobb salad with eggs and white beans
side: Whole-grain crackers or toast on the side.
steps: Put the eggs in a saucepan, cover with cold water and bring to a boil. Turn off the heat, cover and let stand 10 minutes, then move the eggs to a bowl of ice water for 5 minutes. Peel and cut into quarters.
Whisk the Greek yogurt, Dijon, vinegar, olive oil, salt and pepper with 1 tbsp water to make a pourable dressing.
Spread the romaine over a large platter.
Arrange the white beans, cherry tomatoes, avocado, corn, cucumber, cheddar and eggs in rows across the lettuce.
Drizzle with some of the dressing and pass the rest at the table so everyone can toss their own plate.

name: Sheet-pan gochujang tofu with Brussels sprouts
side: Steamed jasmine rice.
mildNote: Use 1 tbsp gochujang and an extra tbsp of honey, or set aside some plain tofu and vegetables before glazing.
steps: Put the rice in a saucepan with 2¼ cups water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low 15 minutes; take it off the heat and let it steam, covered, 10 minutes.

Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the tofu with 2 tbsp of the oil and the cornstarch and spread it over one half of a large sheet pan. Toss the Brussels sprouts and carrots with the last 1 tbsp oil on the other half.
Roast 25 minutes, turning everything once halfway, until the tofu is golden and the sprouts are browned and tender.
Meanwhile whisk the gochujang, soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar and garlic together.
Drizzle the sauce over the pan, toss everything together and roast 5 minutes more, until the glaze is sticky.
Serve over the rice, sprinkled with scallions and sesame seeds.

name: Chickpea salad lettuce wraps with dill
side: Hard-boiled eggs on the side and whole-grain crackers.
steps: Put the eggs in a saucepan, cover with cold water and bring to a boil. Turn off the heat, cover and let stand 10 minutes, then cool in ice water, peel and quarter.
Mash the chickpeas in a bowl with a potato masher or fork until most are broken but some stay chunky.
Stir in the Greek yogurt, Dijon, lemon juice, celery, red onion, dill, salt and pepper.
Spoon the chickpea salad into the lettuce leaves and top with cherry tomatoes.
Serve with the eggs and crackers on the side. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

name: Italian egg drop soup with white beans and spinach
side: Toasted crusty bread.

ingredients.note: finely grated, plus extra to serve

steps: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium-low heat and cook the garlic 1 to 2 minutes, until pale golden.
Add the broth and white beans, bring to a boil, then simmer 5 minutes.
Whisk the eggs, parmesan, lemon zest, nutmeg and pepper together in a bowl.
Stir the spinach into the soup for 1 minute, until wilted. Keep the soup at a steady simmer and slowly pour in the egg mixture while stirring gently with a fork.
Simmer 1 to 2 minutes more, until the egg forms soft, fully cooked ribbons with no runny liquid egg left. Stir in the lemon juice.
Ladle into bowls, top with extra parmesan and serve with the toasted bread.

name: Tandoori-spiced tofu bowls with cucumber yogurt
side: Warm naan alongside.
mildNote: These spices are warm, not hot; for very sensitive eaters use 1 tsp garam masala.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Stir ½ cup of the Greek yogurt with the garam masala, paprika, turmeric, garlic and 1 tsp salt, then gently fold in the tofu until coated.
Toss the cauliflower with the oil and ¼ tsp salt. Spread the tofu and cauliflower on a large sheet pan lined with parchment.
Roast 25 to 30 minutes, turning once, until the tofu is browned at the edges and the cauliflower is tender with charred spots.
Meanwhile put the rice in a saucepan with 2¼ cups water, bring to a boil, cover and simmer on low 15 minutes; rest 5 minutes off the heat.
Stir the remaining 1 cup yogurt with the cucumber and ¼ tsp salt.
Divide the rice among bowls, top with the tofu and cauliflower, add a spoonful of cucumber yogurt and sprinkle with cilantro. Serve with lemon wedges.

name: French lentil and vegetable soup
side: Baguette and a little goat cheese to spread.
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrots and celery with the salt for 8 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the garlic, tomato paste and thyme and cook 2 minutes, until the paste darkens.
Add the lentils, potatoes, bay leaves and broth. Bring to a boil, then partly cover and simmer 25 to 30 minutes, until the lentils and potatoes are tender.
Stir in the kale and simmer 5 minutes more. Remove the bay leaves and taste for salt.
Serve in bowls with sliced baguette. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

name: Rajma (kidney bean curry) with brown rice
side: Cucumber yogurt and lime wedges.
mildNote: Leave out the chili powder and serve with plenty of cucumber yogurt.
steps: Bring a large saucepan of water to a boil, add the brown rice and boil uncovered 30 minutes, until tender; drain and return to the pot, covered.
Meanwhile heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion 10 minutes, until golden.
Add the garlic, ginger, cumin, garam masala and chili powder and stir 1 minute.
Add the crushed tomatoes, kidney beans, 1 cup water and 1 tsp salt. Simmer 20 minutes, stirring now and then, and mash a few beans to thicken the sauce.
Stir the Greek yogurt with the cucumber and ¼ tsp salt.
Serve the rajma over the rice, topped with cilantro and the cucumber yogurt. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

name: Vegetable egg foo young with brown gravy
side: Steamed jasmine rice and sautéed bok choy.
steps: Cook the rice: bring it to a boil with 2¼ cups water, cover and simmer on low 15 minutes, then rest 10 minutes off the heat.

Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat and cook the mushrooms 5 minutes, until browned. Add the cabbage and carrot for 2 minutes, until just wilted. Tip into a bowl to cool for a few minutes.
Whisk the eggs with 1 tbsp of the soy sauce, then stir in the cooked vegetables and scallions.

Heat ½ tbsp oil in the skillet over medium heat. Ladle in about ⅓ cup of egg mixture per patty, 4 at a time, and cook 2 to 3 minutes a side, until golden and set all the way through. Repeat with another ½ tbsp oil to make about 8 patties.
For the gravy, whisk the broth, the remaining 1 tbsp soy sauce, the cornstarch and sugar in a small saucepan and simmer, stirring, 1 to 2 minutes until glossy and thick.
In the same skillet, stir-fry the bok choy with the garlic and the last 1 tbsp oil for 3 minutes, until the stems are crisp-tender.
Serve the egg patties over rice with the gravy spooned on top and the bok choy alongside.

name: Black pepper tofu with bok choy
side: Steamed jasmine rice.
mildNote: Use ½ tsp black pepper; it's the only heat in the dish.
steps: Cook the rice: bring it to a boil with 2¼ cups water, cover and simmer on low 15 minutes, then rest 10 minutes off the heat.
Toss the tofu with the cornstarch. Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat and fry the tofu 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until crisp and golden. Move to a plate.
Add the last 1 tbsp oil, then the bok choy and bell pepper, and stir-fry 3 minutes, until the bok choy stems are crisp-tender.
Add the garlic, ginger and black pepper and stir 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Stir together the soy sauce, brown sugar and 3 tbsp water, pour into the pan, add the tofu and toss 1 minute until glazed.
Serve over the rice, sprinkled with scallions.

name: Zucchini and white bean fritters with lemon yogurt
side: Tomato and cucumber salad.
steps: Toss the grated zucchini with ½ tsp salt in a colander and leave 10 minutes, then squeeze out as much liquid as you can in a clean towel.
Mash the white beans in a large bowl until mostly smooth. Stir in the eggs, flour, feta, scallions, the zucchini and half the dill.

Heat 1½ tbsp olive oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Drop in heaping ¼-cup scoops of batter, flatten to ½ inch and cook 3 to 4 minutes a side, until deep golden and set in the middle. Repeat with another 1½ tbsp oil for the rest (about 12 fritters).
Stir the Greek yogurt with the lemon zest, half the lemon juice, the rest of the dill and a pinch of salt.
Toss the tomatoes and cucumber with the last 1 tbsp olive oil, the rest of the lemon juice and the remaining salt.
Serve the fritters warm with the lemon yogurt and the salad.

name: Edamame crunch bowls with peanut-lime dressing
side: Hard-boiled eggs on top and brown rice underneath.
mildNote: Leave the sriracha out of the dressing and pass it at the table.
steps: Bring a large saucepan of water to a boil, add the brown rice and boil uncovered 30 minutes, until tender, adding the edamame for the last 4 minutes. Drain well.
Meanwhile put the eggs in a small saucepan, cover with cold water and bring to a boil. Turn off the heat, cover and let stand 10 minutes, then cool in ice water, peel and halve.
Whisk the peanut butter, lime juice, soy sauce, honey and sriracha with 2 to 3 tbsp warm water until smooth and pourable.
Toss the red cabbage, carrots, bell pepper and half the cilantro with a third of the dressing.
Divide the rice and edamame among bowls, add the slaw and eggs, drizzle with the rest of the dressing and scatter with peanuts and the remaining cilantro.

name: Crispy chickpea Caesar with roasted broccoli
side: Toasted crusty bread.

ingredients.note: drained, rinsed and patted very dry

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the chickpeas and broccoli on a large sheet pan with 2 tbsp of the olive oil, the garlic powder and ½ tsp salt. Roast 25 minutes, shaking the pan once, until the chickpeas are crisp and the broccoli is charred at the edges.
Meanwhile put the eggs in a saucepan, cover with cold water and bring to a boil. Turn off the heat, cover and let stand 10 minutes, then cool in ice water, peel and quarter.
Whisk the Greek yogurt, half the parmesan, the lemon juice, Dijon, grated garlic, the last 1 tbsp olive oil, the pepper and a pinch of salt with 1 to 2 tbsp water until creamy.
Toss the romaine with most of the dressing.
Top the romaine with the warm broccoli, chickpeas and eggs, drizzle with the rest of the dressing and sprinkle with the remaining parmesan. Serve with the toasted bread.

name: Lemony chicken, white bean and kale soup
side: Toasted crusty bread.
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrots and celery with the salt for 8 minutes, until soft. Stir in the garlic and thyme for 1 minute.

Add the broth and bring to a boil. Lower the whole chicken breasts into the pot (don't rinse raw chicken first), reduce the heat and simmer gently, covered, 15 to 18 minutes, until the thickest part reaches 165°F.
Lift out the chicken onto a cutting board and shred it with two forks. Wash anything that touched the raw chicken.
Add the white beans and kale to the pot and simmer 5 minutes, until the kale is tender.
Return the chicken, stir in the lemon zest and juice and taste for salt.
Serve with the toasted bread. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, simmer a can of white beans and a handful of kale in vegetable broth with a squeeze of lemon in a small pot.

name: Greek chicken and quinoa bowls
side: Warm pita wedges.

ingredients.note: pounded to an even ¾ inch

steps: Put the quinoa in a saucepan with 2 cups water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low 15 minutes. Let stand 5 minutes and fluff.
Rub the chicken with half the lemon juice, 1 tbsp of the olive oil, the oregano, 2 cloves of the garlic and ¾ tsp salt. Wash your hands after handling the raw chicken.
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken 5 to 6 minutes a side, until browned and 165°F in the thickest part. Rest 5 minutes, then slice.
Stir the Greek yogurt with the remaining garlic, the dill and a pinch of salt.
Toss the cucumber, tomatoes, red onion and olives with the rest of the lemon juice, the last 1 tbsp olive oil and the remaining salt.
Divide the quinoa among bowls and top with the chicken, the salad and a spoonful of the dill yogurt. Serve with the warm pita.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, toss a can of chickpeas with a little lemon, oregano and olive oil and use it in place of the chicken.

name: Ground turkey and green bean stir-fry
side: Brown rice.
mildNote: Leave out the chili flakes; the hoisin sauce is sweet and mild.
steps: Bring a large saucepan of water to a boil, add the brown rice and boil uncovered 30 minutes, until tender; drain and keep covered.

Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the green beans and cook 6 to 7 minutes, stirring now and then, until blistered and crisp-tender. Add the bell pepper and onion for 2 minutes, then move everything to a plate.
Add the last 1 tbsp oil and the turkey and cook 6 to 8 minutes, breaking it up, until browned with no pink left and 165°F.
Stir in the garlic, ginger and chili flakes for 30 seconds.
Add the soy sauce, hoisin and rice vinegar, return the vegetables and toss 1 minute until glazed.
Serve over the brown rice, sprinkled with scallions.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, crumble half a block of tofu into a small pan and cook it with a spoonful each of soy sauce and hoisin, then toss with some of the green beans.

name: Turkey and spinach meatballs with roasted vegetables
side: Lemon-garlic yogurt sauce and warm pita.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the zucchini, bell peppers and red onion with the olive oil and ½ tsp salt on a large sheet pan and push them to the edges.

In a bowl mix the turkey, spinach, egg, panko, 2 cloves of the garlic, the oregano, lemon zest and ¾ tsp salt with your hands until just combined. Roll into about 20 golf-ball-size meatballs and set them in the middle of the pan. Wash your hands well.
Roast 20 to 22 minutes, until the meatballs are browned and 165°F in the center and the vegetables are tender.
Stir the Greek yogurt with the lemon juice, the remaining garlic and a pinch of salt.
Serve the meatballs and vegetables with the yogurt sauce and warm pita.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, toss a can of chickpeas with a little oil and oregano and roast them on a corner of the pan with the vegetables.

name: Sheet-pan lemon cod with green beans and tomatoes
side: Quinoa or crusty bread to soak up the juices.
steps: Put the quinoa in a saucepan with 2 cups water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low 15 minutes; let stand 5 minutes and fluff.
Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the green beans, cherry tomatoes, white beans and garlic with 2 tbsp of the olive oil and ½ tsp salt on a sheet pan. Roast 10 minutes.
Rub the cod with the last 1 tbsp olive oil, the lemon zest, paprika, the rest of the salt and the pepper.
Push the vegetables aside, lay the cod on the pan and roast 10 to 12 minutes, until the fish reaches 145°F and flakes easily with a fork.
Squeeze a couple of lemon wedges over the pan, scatter with parsley and serve with the quinoa and remaining lemon wedges.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, set aside a second can of white beans to roast with the vegetables and skip the fish on their plates.

name: Tilapia with mango salsa, black beans and brown rice
side: Lime wedges and sliced avocado.
mildNote: Season the fish with cumin only and skip the chili powder for kids.
steps: Bring a large saucepan of water to a boil, add the brown rice and boil uncovered 30 minutes, until tender; drain, stir in the black beans and ¼ tsp salt and cover to keep warm.
Toss the mango, bell pepper, red onion, cilantro, lime juice and ¼ tsp salt together for the salsa.
Mix the chili powder, cumin and remaining salt and sprinkle over both sides of the tilapia.
Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the fish 3 minutes a side, until it is opaque, flakes easily with a fork and reaches 145°F.
Serve the tilapia over the rice and beans with the mango salsa and avocado.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, warm an extra can of black beans with a pinch of cumin and pile it high with the mango salsa.

name: Salmon quinoa bowls with cucumber and lemon-dill yogurt
side: Extra lemon wedges.
steps: Put the quinoa in a saucepan with 3 cups water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low 15 minutes; let stand 5 minutes and fluff.

Heat the oven to 425°F. Set the salmon skin side down on a lined sheet pan, rub with 1 tbsp of the olive oil, half the lemon zest, ½ tsp salt and the pepper. Roast 12 to 14 minutes, until it reaches 145°F and flakes easily.
Stir the Greek yogurt with half the dill, the garlic, the rest of the lemon zest, 1 tbsp lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Toss the warm quinoa with the spinach so it wilts slightly, then add the cucumber, tomatoes, chickpeas, the rest of the lemon juice, the last 1 tbsp olive oil and the remaining salt.
Divide the quinoa salad among bowls, flake the salmon over the top, add a spoonful of dill yogurt and scatter with the remaining dill.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, top their bowls with an extra can of chickpeas and a couple of hard-boiled eggs instead of salmon.

name: Lemon-pepper shrimp and asparagus sheet pan with quinoa
side: A green salad.
steps: Put the quinoa in a saucepan with 3 cups water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low 15 minutes; let stand 5 minutes and fluff.
Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the asparagus and bell peppers with 2 tbsp of the olive oil and ½ tsp salt on a large sheet pan and roast 10 minutes.
Toss the shrimp with the last 1 tbsp olive oil, the lemon zest, black pepper, garlic and remaining salt.
Spread the shrimp over the vegetables and roast 6 to 8 minutes, until the shrimp are pink and opaque all the way through.
Squeeze the lemon juice over the pan and toss with the parsley.
Serve over the quinoa with the feta crumbled on top.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, roast a can of chickpeas with the vegetables from the start and keep them off the shrimp side.

name: Lemon-garlic chicken with broccoli and white beans
side: Crusty bread.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the broccoli, white beans and red onion with 2 tbsp of the olive oil and ½ tsp salt on a large sheet pan.

In a bowl toss the chicken with the last 1 tbsp olive oil, the garlic, lemon zest, Italian seasoning, remaining salt and the pepper. Don't rinse the raw chicken; wash your hands and the board after handling it.
Nestle the chicken among the vegetables in a single layer and roast 20 to 22 minutes, turning once, until the chicken is browned and 165°F inside and the broccoli is charred at the edges.
Squeeze the lemon juice over everything and sprinkle with the parmesan.
Serve straight from the pan with crusty bread.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, roast the beans and vegetables on a separate small pan; add a few eggs, hard-boiled, for extra protein.

name: Chicken and black bean burrito salad
side: Tortilla chips for crunch.
mildNote: Use 1 tsp chili powder on the chicken; it's warm rather than hot.

ingredients.note: pounded to an even ¾ inch

steps: Rub the chicken with the chili powder, cumin and ¾ tsp salt. Wash your hands after handling the raw chicken.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the chicken 5 to 6 minutes a side, until 165°F in the thickest part. Rest 5 minutes, then slice.
In the same skillet cook the corn 3 minutes, until lightly charred, then add the black beans for 1 minute to warm.
Whisk the Greek yogurt, lime juice, half the cilantro and the remaining salt with 1 to 2 tbsp water to make a creamy dressing.
Pile the romaine into bowls and top with the corn and beans, tomatoes, avocado and chicken.
Drizzle with the dressing and finish with the rest of the cilantro and the tortilla chips.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, double the beans on their salads with a second warmed can of black beans.

name: Ginger chicken congee with bok choy
side: Soft-boiled eggs and soy sauce at the table.

ingredients.note: half sliced, half cut in thin matchsticks

steps: Put the rice, broth, 3 cups water, sliced ginger, garlic and salt in a large pot and bring to a boil.

Add the chicken thighs (don't rinse them first), lower the heat and simmer gently, partly covered, 20 to 25 minutes, until the chicken reaches 165°F. Lift out the chicken and shred it; wash the board and your hands.
Keep simmering the rice another 20 to 25 minutes, stirring often so it doesn't stick, until thick, creamy and broken down. Add water if it gets too thick.
Meanwhile lower the eggs into a pot of boiling water and cook 7 minutes, then cool in cold water, peel and halve.
Remove the ginger slices, stir in the bok choy and shredded chicken and simmer 3 to 4 minutes, until the bok choy is tender.
Serve in bowls topped with the ginger matchsticks, scallions, eggs, a drizzle of soy sauce and sesame oil. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, simmer a small pot of rice in vegetable broth and water with a few slices of ginger the same way, adding cubed tofu and some of the bok choy at the end.

name: Turkey, sweet potato and kale skillet
side: Fried or soft-scrambled eggs on top for the hungriest.
mildNote: Smoked paprika is smoky rather than hot; use 1 tsp for very cautious eaters.
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the sweet potato and ½ tsp salt, cover and cook 8 to 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until nearly tender.
Add the onion and bell pepper, uncover and cook 5 minutes.
Push the vegetables to the side, add the turkey and cook 6 to 8 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reaches 165°F.
Stir in the garlic, smoked paprika, cumin, sage and remaining salt for 1 minute.
Add the kale with 2 tbsp water and cook 3 minutes, until wilted and the sweet potato is fork-tender.
Serve with a spoonful of Greek yogurt on each plate.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, cook a can of black beans with a little smoked paprika in a small pan and fold it into some of the sweet potato and kale before adding the turkey.

name: Herb pork tenderloin with roasted carrots and Brussels sprouts
side: Apple-mustard yogurt sauce and crusty bread.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the Brussels sprouts and carrots with 2 tbsp of the olive oil and ½ tsp salt on a large sheet pan and roast 10 minutes.
Mix the last 1 tbsp olive oil, the rosemary, thyme, garlic, 1 tbsp of the Dijon, remaining salt and the pepper, and rub it all over the pork.
Push the vegetables to the edges, set the pork in the middle and roast 20 to 25 minutes, turning the vegetables once, until the pork reaches 145°F in the thickest part.
Rest the pork 5 minutes (at least 3), then slice into medallions.
Stir the Greek yogurt, honey and the rest of the Dijon together and serve with the pork and vegetables.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, roast a can of chickpeas with the vegetables and serve them with the honey-mustard yogurt.

name: Sirloin and charred corn salad with lime
side: Warm corn tortillas.
mildNote: Skip the chili powder on the steak and season it with salt and pepper only.
steps: Rub the steak with the chili powder and ½ tsp salt.

Heat 1 tbsp of the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear the steak 4 to 5 minutes a side, until it reaches 145°F in the center. Rest it on a board at least 3 minutes, then slice thinly across the grain.
In the same skillet cook the corn kernels 4 to 5 minutes, until charred in spots, then stir in the black beans to warm.
Whisk the lime juice, remaining 2 tbsp olive oil and remaining salt in a large bowl. Add the romaine, tomatoes, red onion, cilantro and the warm corn and beans and toss.
Top with the steak and avocado. Warm the tortillas in the skillet for 30 seconds a side and serve alongside.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, warm a second can of black beans and add it to their salads in place of the steak.

name: Korean-style chicken lettuce wraps
side: Jasmine rice and quick-pickled cucumbers.
mildNote: Use 2 tsp gochujang, or set aside some chicken tossed only with soy sauce and honey.
steps: Cook the rice: bring it to a boil with 2¼ cups water, cover and simmer on low 15 minutes, then rest 10 minutes off the heat.
Toss the cucumbers with the rice vinegar and set aside to pickle.
Stir the gochujang, soy sauce, honey, garlic and ginger together.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken 7 to 8 minutes, stirring, until browned and 165°F inside. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw chicken.
Add the sauce and toss 1 to 2 minutes, until sticky.
Spoon rice and chicken into lettuce leaves and top with carrots, pickled cucumbers, scallions and sesame seeds.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, cook cubed tofu in a small pan and toss it with a spoonful of the sauce before the chicken goes in.

name: Chicken, snap pea and carrot stir-fry
side: Brown rice.
steps: Bring a large saucepan of water to a boil, add the brown rice and boil uncovered 30 minutes, until tender; drain and keep covered.
Toss the chicken with 1 tbsp of the cornstarch and 1 tbsp of the soy sauce. Stir the rest of the soy sauce, the honey, the rest of the cornstarch and ½ cup water together for the sauce.
Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over high heat. Stir-fry the chicken 5 to 6 minutes, until golden and 165°F inside. Move to a plate and wash anything that touched the raw chicken.
Add the last 1 tbsp oil, the carrots, snap peas and bell pepper and stir-fry 3 to 4 minutes, until crisp-tender. Add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.
Return the chicken, pour in the sauce and stir 1 to 2 minutes until it thickens and coats everything. Drizzle with the sesame oil.
Serve over the brown rice.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, stir-fry cubed tofu in a small pan and toss it with a little of the sauce and some of the vegetables.

name: Cod foil packets with zucchini, tomatoes and olives
side: Couscous.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Tear off 4 large sheets of foil.

Divide the zucchini among the foil sheets, top each with a cod fillet, then the tomatoes, olives, garlic and lemon slices. Drizzle each with ½ tbsp olive oil and sprinkle with the oregano and ½ tsp salt in total.

Fold the foil over and crimp the edges tightly to make sealed packets. Set them on a sheet pan and bake 15 to 18 minutes, until the fish reaches 145°F and flakes easily (open one carefully to check; watch for steam).

Meanwhile bring 1½ cups water, the last 1 tbsp olive oil and the remaining salt to a boil, stir in the couscous and chickpeas, cover and take off the heat for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork and stir in half the parsley.
Serve the packets on plates over the couscous, spooning the juices over and scattering with the rest of the parsley.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, make a packet with extra vegetables and a can of white beans instead of the fish; it bakes in the same time.

name: Turkey-zucchini burgers with sweet potato wedges
side: Lettuce, tomato and a quick yogurt-mustard sauce.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the sweet potato wedges with 2 tbsp of the olive oil, the paprika and ½ tsp salt on a sheet pan and roast 30 to 35 minutes, turning once, until browned and tender.
Mix the turkey, zucchini, panko, garlic powder and remaining salt with your hands and shape into 4 patties about ¾ inch thick, pressing a dimple in the middle of each. Wash your hands well.
Heat the last 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the burgers 5 to 6 minutes a side, until they reach 165°F in the center.
Stir the Greek yogurt and Dijon together for the sauce.
Serve the burgers in the toasted buns with lettuce, tomato and the yogurt-mustard sauce, with the sweet potato wedges alongside.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, mash a can of white beans with a spoonful of the panko and some grated zucchini, form a patty and pan-fry it 3 to 4 minutes a side.

name: Chili-lime chicken with zucchini, corn and black beans
side: Warm corn tortillas and a spoonful of Greek yogurt.
mildNote: Use 1 tsp chili powder; the yogurt cools it further.
steps: Toss the chicken with the chili powder, cumin, lime zest and salt. Wash your hands after handling the raw chicken.
Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken 7 to 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until browned and 165°F inside. Move to a plate.
Add the last 1 tbsp oil, the onion and zucchini and cook 5 minutes, until the zucchini is browned in spots. Add the corn and garlic and cook 3 minutes more.
Stir in the black beans and the chicken with its juices and cook 2 minutes to heat through. Take off the heat and stir in the lime juice and cilantro.
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet for 30 seconds a side and serve with the skillet and the Greek yogurt.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, cook the vegetables and an extra can of black beans in a small pan with the same spices.

name: Garlic-ginger shrimp with snap peas and peppers
side: Brown rice.
steps: Bring a large saucepan of water to a boil, add the brown rice and boil uncovered 30 minutes, until tender; drain and keep covered.
Stir the soy sauce, honey, cornstarch, rice vinegar and ⅓ cup water together for the sauce.
Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over high heat. Stir-fry the snap peas and bell peppers 3 minutes, until crisp-tender, then move to a plate.
Add the last 1 tbsp oil and the shrimp and cook 1½ to 2 minutes a side, until pink and opaque all the way through. Add the garlic, ginger and scallions for 30 seconds.
Return the vegetables, pour in the sauce and stir 1 minute, until thick and glossy.
Serve over the brown rice.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, stir-fry cubed tofu in a small pan and toss it with some of the vegetables and a little of the sauce.

name: Cumin pork tenderloin with roasted cauliflower and chickpeas
side: Herby yogurt sauce and warm pita.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Mix the cumin, coriander and paprika.
Toss the cauliflower, chickpeas and onion with 2 tbsp of the olive oil, half the spice mix and ½ tsp salt on a large sheet pan. Roast 10 minutes.
Rub the pork with the last 1 tbsp olive oil, the rest of the spice mix and ½ tsp salt.

Push the vegetables to the edges, set the pork in the middle and roast 20 to 25 minutes, stirring the vegetables once, until the pork reaches 145°F in the thickest part. Rest it at least 3 minutes, then slice.
Stir the Greek yogurt with the mint, lemon juice and the remaining salt.
Serve the pork, cauliflower and chickpeas with the yogurt sauce and warm pita.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, roast an extra can of chickpeas with the vegetables and serve them with the mint yogurt.

name: Sheet-pan Dijon salmon with green beans and chickpeas
side: Brown rice or crusty bread.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the green beans, chickpeas and shallots with 2 tbsp of the olive oil and ½ tsp salt on a large sheet pan and roast 10 minutes.
Stir the Dijon, honey, garlic, the last 1 tbsp olive oil, the remaining salt and the pepper together.
Push the vegetables aside, lay the salmon skin side down on the pan and spread the mustard mixture over the top.
Roast 12 to 14 minutes, until the salmon reaches 145°F and flakes easily and the green beans are tender with browned spots.
Scatter with dill and serve with lemon wedges.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, roast an extra can of chickpeas and some cubed tofu brushed with a little of the mustard glaze.

name: Unstuffed turkey cabbage roll skillet
side: A dollop of Greek yogurt and dill.
steps: Bring a saucepan of water to a boil, add the brown rice and boil uncovered 25 minutes, until nearly tender; drain.
Meanwhile heat the olive oil in a large deep skillet or pot over medium-high heat. Cook the turkey and onion 7 to 8 minutes, breaking up the meat, until no pink remains and it reaches 165°F.
Stir in the garlic, carrots and paprika for 1 minute.
Add the cabbage, diced tomatoes, tomato sauce, broth, salt and the rice. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low 15 minutes, stirring once, until the cabbage is tender and the rice is cooked.
Stir in half the dill and serve with a spoonful of Greek yogurt and the rest of the dill on top. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, simmer a can of white beans with a few ladles of the cabbage, tomato and rice before adding the meat (cook the vegetables in vegetable broth for this portion).

name: Curry-roasted chicken thighs with cauliflower and carrots
side: Herb yogurt and warm naan.
mildNote: Use a mild curry powder; the herb yogurt cools it for kids.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the chicken with ¼ cup of the Greek yogurt, 1 tbsp of the curry powder, the garlic and ¾ tsp salt. Don't rinse raw chicken; wash your hands after handling it.
Toss the cauliflower, carrots and onion with 2 tbsp of the oil, the rest of the curry powder and ½ tsp salt on a large sheet pan.
Nestle the chicken among the vegetables, drizzle with the last 1 tbsp oil and roast 25 to 30 minutes, until the chicken is browned and 165°F inside and the vegetables are tender.
Stir the remaining Greek yogurt with the cilantro, mint, lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Warm the naan in the oven for the last 3 minutes and serve with the chicken, vegetables and herb yogurt.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, toss a can of chickpeas in a little oil and curry powder and roast them on a corner of the pan.

name: Lemon-dill tilapia with roasted asparagus and potatoes
side: Greek yogurt tartar-style sauce.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the potatoes with 2 tbsp of the olive oil and ½ tsp salt on a large sheet pan and roast 20 minutes.
Add the asparagus to the pan, toss it in the oil on the pan, and push everything to the edges.
Lay the tilapia in the middle, brush with the last 1 tbsp olive oil and sprinkle with the lemon zest, half the dill, the garlic powder, the pepper and ½ tsp salt.
Roast 10 to 12 minutes, until the fish is opaque, flakes easily and reaches 145°F and the potatoes are golden and tender.
Stir the Greek yogurt with the capers, the rest of the dill, 1 tbsp lemon juice and the remaining salt.
Squeeze the rest of the lemon juice over the fish and vegetables and serve with the sauce.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, roast a can of white beans tossed with lemon zest and dill on the pan in place of the fish.

name: Thai-style chicken and cabbage salad with peanut-lime dressing
side: Rice noodles or jasmine rice for anyone who wants more.
mildNote: Leave the sriracha out of the dressing and pass it at the table.
steps: Put the chicken in a saucepan, cover with cold water, add the salt and bring to a gentle simmer. Cover and simmer on low 12 to 15 minutes, until the thickest part reaches 165°F. Don't rinse raw chicken first.
Let the chicken cool 5 minutes on a board, then shred it with two forks.
Whisk the peanut butter, lime juice, soy sauce, honey and sriracha with 2 to 3 tbsp warm water until smooth.
Toss both cabbages, the carrots, cucumber, cilantro and mint in a large bowl with most of the dressing.
Top with the chicken, drizzle with the rest of the dressing and scatter with the peanuts.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, toss a bowl of the slaw with cooked edamame instead of chicken.

name: Shrimp, corn and avocado chopped salad
side: Tortilla chips or warm corn tortillas.
steps: Heat 1 tbsp of the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the corn 4 minutes, until charred in spots; tip into a large bowl.
Toss the shrimp with the paprika, garlic and ½ tsp salt. Add another 1 tbsp olive oil to the skillet and cook the shrimp 1½ to 2 minutes a side, until pink and opaque all the way through.
Whisk the lime juice, the last 1 tbsp olive oil and the remaining salt into the bowl with the corn.
Add the romaine, black beans, tomatoes, cucumber and cilantro and toss well.
Top with the avocado and shrimp and serve with tortilla chips.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, add an extra can of black beans and a couple of hard-boiled eggs to their salads instead of shrimp.

name: Barbecue chicken-stuffed sweet potatoes with crunchy slaw
side: Extra slaw on the side.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Prick the sweet potatoes with a fork, set them on a foil-lined sheet pan and bake 45 to 55 minutes, until very soft when squeezed.
Meanwhile stir the tomato sauce, brown sugar, 3 tbsp of the cider vinegar, the smoked paprika, garlic powder and ½ tsp salt in a saucepan and bring to a simmer.

Add the whole chicken breasts (don't rinse them first), cover and simmer on low 18 to 20 minutes, turning once, until the chicken reaches 165°F. Shred it in the pot with two forks and simmer 5 minutes more to thicken.
Toss the cabbage and carrots with the Greek yogurt, the last 1 tbsp cider vinegar and the remaining salt.
Split the sweet potatoes open, fluff the insides, pile on the barbecue chicken and top with slaw and scallions.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, simmer a can of pinto beans in a small pot with a few spoonfuls of the barbecue sauce before adding the chicken.
